criterion: The marketing pages and the studio sit on one near-black ground with a single saturated blue carrying every interactive thing.
evaluation_rule: Yes if every page in the product uses one near-black surface as its ground and exactly one saturated hue appears on links, focus states and primary actions. No if a second saturated hue appears in the chrome, or if the ground is a light surface.

criterion: One cool neutral ladder carries hierarchy across the marketing pages and the studio, with a light vivid cyan reserved for in-body links.
evaluation_rule: A LADDER is a set of named neutral steps from lightest to darkest. Yes if secondary text, dividers and disabled states all draw from one neutral ladder, and a link inside body copy is a cyan distinct from the brand blue. No if a second grey family appears alongside the first, or if in-body links use the same hue as the primary action.

criterion: One accent sweep on the marketing pages runs from a light vivid indigo into the brand blue, and that indigo is confined to that one sweep.
evaluation_rule: Yes if exactly one gradient in the product runs from an indigo into the brand blue, and every other surface stays within the neutral ladder and the blue ramp. No if the indigo shows up outside that one sweep, or if the product carries no such sweep.

criterion: Corner softness on the marketing pages and in the studio is graded, running from barely softened utility chips through cards to pill-shaped buttons.
evaluation_rule: Yes if at least three distinct corner radii are visible across chips, cards and controls, and buttons read as pills. No if every corner shares one radius, or if a control other than a button reads as a pill.

criterion: One cool-grey shadow lifts a dropdown panel in the marketing navigation and a smaller floating panel in the studio, leaving every other surface flat.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a dropdown carries a deeper shadow, smaller floating panels carry a shallower one, and every other surface is flat. No if cards or bands carry shadows, or if the shadow reads as neutral black rather than cool grey.

criterion: Every illustration on the marketing pages and in the studio is drawn or generated by code, with placeholder customer marks and a globe composed from primitives.
evaluation_rule: Yes if no photographic or vector image file is loaded anywhere and every mark, plate, texture and mesh is produced by the running product. No if any illustration is a stored image file, or if a customer mark is anything other than a generated placeholder.

criterion: Icons across the chrome and the map are line drawings at one stroke thickness inheriting the colour of the text around them.
evaluation_rule: Yes if every icon reads as a single-weight line drawing and takes its colour from the surrounding text rather than carrying its own. No if an icon is filled artwork, or if icons vary in stroke thickness between surfaces.

criterion: The live map floats three control clusters over the canvas, and the active scene row is marked by more than colour.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the scene rail, the lighting panel and the colour-theme panel all sit over the map rather than beside it, and the selected scene carries a mark beyond a colour change. No if a panel sits outside the map, or if selection is signalled by colour alone.

criterion: Each marketing page and each studio surface leads with a single primary action that is visually distinct from every secondary one.
evaluation_rule: A PRIMARY ACTION is the one thing the page most wants somebody to do, such as the sign-up control on a marketing page or the New control in the studio. Yes if exactly one control per page wears the strongest treatment. No if two or more controls share the strongest treatment on one page.

criterion: Buttons, chips and map controls each show a resting, a pointed-at, a pressed, a focused and an unavailable appearance, with unavailability carrying more than a colour change.
evaluation_rule: Yes if pointing at, pressing and focusing one of these controls each changes how it looks, and an unavailable control is marked by something beyond colour. No if any of the five states looks identical to another, or if unavailability is signalled by colour alone.

criterion: A refused row in the studio returns to its previous value and says why beside the row rather than elsewhere on the page.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a rejected edit restores the value the row held before and shows its reason next to that row. No if the row keeps the rejected value, or if the reason appears only in a corner of the page.

criterion: Focus moves into a studio dialogue when one opens, and an operation committed by another member is announced as the operation arrives.
evaluation_rule: ANNOUNCED means a screen reader speaks the change without the reader moving focus. Yes if opening a dialogue puts focus inside it, closing it returns focus to the opener, the map responds to pan, zoom and rotate keys, and a remote operation is spoken. No if focus stays behind an open dialogue, or a remote operation changes the canvas silently.

criterion: Movement across the marketing pages and the studio shares one eased character, and a reduced-motion preference settles every continuous motion.
evaluation_rule: EASED means movement leaves quickly and arrives slowly. Yes if movement across both surfaces reads as one family, and a reduced-motion preference stops the logo strip, the shimmer and the map ripple. No if one surface moves with a visibly different character, or a continuous motion keeps running under that preference.

criterion: Body text meets WCAG AA contrast against the near-black ground, with every control reachable by keyboard navigation under a visible focus indicator.
evaluation_rule: Yes if body copy clears the WCAG AA contrast bar on every surface and a keyboard alone reaches every control with an indicator visible at each stop that is not carried by colour alone. No if body copy sits below the bar anywhere, or a control is reachable only by pointer.

criterion: At tablet width the marketing navigation centre collapses into one toggle with the sign-up control still in reach, and every page keeps its content inside the window at every width.
evaluation_rule: Yes if narrowing to tablet width leaves a single menu toggle beside a visible sign-up control, and every page keeps its content inside the window at every width between phone and desk. No if the menu stays expanded at tablet width, or a page grows a sideways scrollbar at some width.

criterion: Decoration stands in place of product information on a marketing band.
evaluation_rule: DECORATION is artwork or ornament occupying space that carries no product information. Yes if a marketing band is filled with ornament where the product information belongs. No if every band carries product information in the space it occupies.

criterion: The live map is presented as a still image rather than a surface the visitor can move.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the home page shows a fixed picture of a map that does not respond to a drag. No if the map responds to a drag by re-rendering.
